To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

postsynaptic activation of group II metabotopic glutamate receptors (linked to phospholipases C and D) increases postsynaptic Ca(2+) concentration and induces long-term depression (via protein kinase C) of excitatory synapses on rat prefrontal pyramidal neurons.

DCG IV induces LTD through postsynaptically activated group II mGLuRs that are linked to phospholippases C and D and that activate PKC, which in turn increases postsynaptic Ca 2+ levels through IP3 receptor-mediated Ca2+ release from intracellular stores, and that the Ca2+ rises are required for DCG IV-induced long-term depression of layer I to layer V pyrarmidal neuron glutametergic synapses.
postsynaptic mGluR2 and mGluR3 activation induces LTD through postsynaptically increased IP3 and Ca2+concentrations, and through PKC activation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of long-lasting synaptic changes in the prefrontal cortex that may underlie the development of cognitive deficits associated with neuropsychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia.
a novel type of LTD induced by the activation of presynaptic group II metabotropic receptors, and the mechanisms of the LTD are similar to those of NMDA receptor-dependent Ca2+-dependent LTD.
the role of group II mGlur-mediated LTD in the prefrontal cortex, a brain region that is critically involved in working memory, and the mechanisms of this LTD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
group II mGLuRs, linked to PLC, IP3, PKC, and Ca2+ rises, induce LTD in rat medial prefrontcortex.
postsynaptic mGluRs linked to phospholapase C and probably phospholipaseD induce LTD through postsnaptic PKC activation, and IP3receptors and postsynaptic Ca+ rises.

DCG IV-induced group II mGLuR-mediated LTD in prefrontal cortex is a postsynaptic Ca-dependent LTD, which requires small NMDA-mediated synaptic responses, and which is mediated by phospholipase-C and -D, PKC and PKA, and IP3 receptor activation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
postsynaptic mGluRs linked to phospholipses C and/or D induce LTD through PKC and Ca2+-dependent mechanisms in the rat medial prefrontcortical pyramidal neurons.
group II mGLuRs induce LTD through postsynthesis of IP3 and DAG by activation of phospholipase Cs and Ds.
postsynaptic mGluR-mediated LTD in rat prefrontal cortex is mediated by group II mGLuRs linked to phospholipo-lase C/IP3receptor, phospholipases A2/D, PKC, and Ca2+ rises.
The main takeaway from our work is that
postsynaptic mGluR2/3-mediated LTD is mediated by a postsynaptic signaling pathway involving PLC, IP3, and PKC.

group II mGLuRs are capable of inducing long-term depression of excitatory synaptic transmission in rat prefrontal cortex, and that this depression requires activation of phospholipase-C, phospholipid-D, PKC, and IP3 receptors.
group II mGlutamate receptors are involved in the long-term depression of synaptic strength in the prefrontal cortex.
